title: Adaptive Sprint Buffer and Minimum Viable Slice Plan
creator: Priya Raman
description: Objective: Define a lightweight, repeatable approach for reserving and deploying an adaptive sprint buffer (time and headcount) plus a clear minimum-viable-slice (MVS) decomposition pattern used during cycle triage. The playbook should enable PMs and Eng leads to make fast scope-cut decisions that protect critical SLAs (latency/SLOs, Dedicated commit paths) while keeping customer-facing work moving. Scope: guidance for calculating buffer size, prioritization rubric for what gets cut vs deferred, sample MVS templates for common Redwood initiatives (runtime perf, console UX, Dedicated capacity), and a short ops checklist for handoffs to on-call/incident owners. Excludes: long-term hiring plans and multi-cycle roadmap changes.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Playbook doc exists with a formulaic buffer sizing recommendation and worked examples for small/medium/large initiatives.
A2: MVS templates created for at least three initiative types (runtime, console, Dedicated) and stored in Confluence.
A3: Triage rubric (impact, risk, unblockability, cross-team cost) approved by Eng leads and PMG.
A4: One pilot cycle run using the playbook with a post-mortem and at least two measurable outcomes (reduced mid-cycle scope churn, preserved SLA spend).
comments: 2026-02-15 — Priya Raman: Initial draft of objectives and scope. Shared prototype buffer sizing formula: floor(max(3, ceil(0.15 * planned_story_points))) plus a 10% contingency for external dependencies. Asked Eng leads for feasibility feedback.
